title: Evaluation of the A-STAM and WAI-V for assessing the Therapeutic Alliance in the Treatment of Aphasia
summary:
This study is about the collaboration between people with aphasia and their therapists. This collaboration is called therapeutic alliance. We want to find out more about therapeutic alliance in speech therapy treatment for aphasia.
We want to find out:
1.	How reliably can therapeutic alliance be measured using two questionnaires?
2.	Are there any correlations between the therapeutic alliance and other factors (e.g. the number of sessions or the severity of the aphasia)?
3.	How do people with aphasia and their therapists experience the therapeutic alliance?
The measuring instruments used in this study are questionnaires. The two questionnaires are called:
•	A-STAM: Aphasia and Stroke Therapeutic Alliance Measure 
•	WAI-V: Working Alliance Inventory – Simplified
The A-STAM is a questionnaire on therapeutic alliance in aphasia after a stroke.
The WAI-V is a simplified version of a questionnaire on therapeutic alliance in psychotherapy.
We know from other studies on psychotherapy that the psychotherapeutic relationship makes a significant and consistent contribution to the success of treatment. That is why we want to better understand and measure therapeutic alliance in speech therapy.
The results will later be used in research, practice and training.
Patients with aphasia and their speech therapists can participate in this study together.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Therapists:
▪ Completed vocational training and/or degree in speech therapy, clinical linguistics or comparable qualification
▪ Work in an outpatient setting

Patients:
▪ Presence of aphasia caused by a stroke
▪ Legal age
▪ At least moderate language comprehension (minimum T-score of 44 in the language comprehension subtest of the Aachen Aphasia Test; Huber et al., 1983)
▪ Sufficient visual and hearing function (sufficiently supported by glasses or hearing aids, if necessary)
▪ For the test-retest reliability subgroup (n = 30): chronic phase of aphasia (> 6 months); otherwise, inclusion of individuals in all phases

For therapists and patients together:
▪ Currently and for at least two therapy sessions in speech therapy treatment
Exclusion criteria:
People who do not meet the inclusion criteria will be excluded.
